newsitem.title: BELGIUM: KOREAN KIA INTEREST IN BELGIAN RENAULT PLANT - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: KOREAN KIA INTEREST IN BELGIAN RENAULT PLANT - PAPER.

text.p: South Korean car maker KIA is considering buying the Belgian car assembly plant of French Renault SA , Belgian financial daily De Financieel-Economische Tijd said on Thursday.

Jong Chung, KIA Motors Europe's managing director, told the paper at the Geneva car show that the car maker first had to review the books at Renault Industrie Belgique in Vilvoorde near Brussels before making a definitive decision.
He said KIA would be seeking output of 150,000 cars a year, which would mean the plant would run at full capacity. He did not say which model KIA would be making there.

Renault spokesman Patrick Bessy told the paper at the car show, "We are happy with any producer, any industrialist coming forward as a candidate for a takeover. It does not make a difference who it is as long as there is a takeover."
The FET quoted Chrysler Europe spokeswoman Erika Huyck as saying talk that the U.S. car maker would be interested in Renault Vilvoorde was "rumours which we deny completely."
KIA was aiming to strengthen its competitive position in Europe with a Belgian production unit. "We mainly want to compete in the mid-class car range with Opel , Ford and Volkswagen ," Chung said.
He noted wage costs in Belgium were lower than costs in Germany where KIA has a contract with ~Wilhelm Karmann~which assembles the KIA Sportage.
A production unit in Korea involved high transport costs and import duties, he added.

Renault said last Thursday it would close its Vilvoorde plant in July with a loss of 3,100 jobs as part of a restructuring following heavy losses. It said it would actively look for a car maker interested in taking over the plant.

The unexpected closure news has sparked a storm of protest from unions, but also French and Belgian governments, who have lashed out at the harsh way Renault made the announcement without apparently considering the social consequences.
